scope: Native macOS apps built with SwiftUI or AppKit, including menu bar extras. Other Apple platforms are out of scope.

normalText.note: Text up to 17 pt in a regular or lighter weight. Accessibility Inspector uses this WCAG AA value.

largeText.note: Text of 18 pt or larger, or bold text of any size.

nonText.note: Apple gives no separate number for icons, control boundaries, and state indicators. This WCAG 2.2 AA value is used for them.

targets.note: Pass or fail uses the minimum control size. The default control size is reported as advice.

requirements.title: Purpose
requirements.criterion: Each view and control serves a clear goal of the person, and the most important outcome is obvious first.

requirements.title: Agency
requirements.criterion: People stay informed about what is happening, can act in their own way, and can recover from mistakes.

requirements.title: Responsibility
requirements.criterion: The interface is transparent about what it does and why, protects data, and never presents false success.

requirements.title: Familiarity
requirements.criterion: Controls use familiar platform patterns, behave consistently, and give clear feedback.

requirements.title: Flexibility
requirements.criterion: The interface works with the supported inputs, abilities, appearances, and window sizes, and preserves context.

requirements.title: Simplicity
requirements.criterion: Every element earns its place, copy is concise, and hierarchy makes the next step clear.

requirements.title: Craft
requirements.criterion: Visual, wording, and state details are precise and stay correct while loading, resizing, and failing.

requirements.title: Delight
requirements.criterion: Character comes from usefulness and care, not from decoration that competes with the task.

requirements.title: Menu bar extra symbol
requirements.criterion: The menu bar extra uses a symbol or template icon defined by black and clear areas, so the system can tint it for light and dark menu bars and the selected state. It fits the 24 pt menu bar and has an accessibility label.

requirements.title: Menu before window style
requirements.criterion: Clicking the extra shows a menu. A popover-like window (SwiftUI MenuBarExtra window style) is used only when the content is too complex or data rich for a menu, and the audit records that reason.

requirements.title: Not the only path
requirements.criterion: The app does not depend on its extra being visible. The system can hide extras, so important functions are also reachable another way, such as a window.

requirements.title: People decide on the extra
requirements.criterion: People, not the app, decide whether the extra is in the menu bar. For a menu-bar-only app, removing the extra quits the app, and the app documents how to get it back.

requirements.title: Window behavior
requirements.criterion: Windows resize fluidly to sensible minimum sizes, keep their state, use the system main, key, and inactive appearances, have a useful title that is not only the app name, and avoid custom window chrome.

requirements.title: Nothing critical at the bottom
requirements.criterion: Critical information and actions are not placed at the bottom of a window or sidebar, because a window can extend below the display.

requirements.title: Sidebar structure
requirements.criterion: A sidebar shows no more than two levels, uses familiar symbols with purposeful colors, highlights the current selection, and can be hidden.

requirements.title: Toolbar items
requirements.criterion: Toolbar items are few and deliberate, use standard components and system symbols without borders, have accessibility labels, group by function, and are also available as menu commands when the app has a menu bar.

requirements.title: Lists and tables
requirements.criterion: Row text is succinct and not clipped without a way to read it. Multicolumn tables have descriptive headings, sort by column when useful, allow column resizing, and use an outline view for hierarchy.

requirements.title: Switches and checkboxes
requirements.criterion: Switches and checkboxes sit in the window body, not the frame. A switch is used for an emphasized setting, a mini switch for a single row in a grouped form, and a checkbox for a hierarchy of settings. State differences are obvious.

requirements.title: Alerts and confirmations
requirements.criterion: Alerts are rare and reserved for consequential actions that cannot be undone. Titles describe the situation directly and button labels name the action.

requirements.title: Progress and loading
requirements.criterion: Progress is determinate when the app knows it, appears in a consistent place, lets people halt work when feasible, and content shows as soon as possible. A project contract may replace animated indicators with static status.

requirements.title: Keyboard shortcuts and Full Keyboard Access
requirements.criterion: Standard shortcuts keep their meaning, custom shortcuts exist only for frequent commands, displayed shortcuts work, and every task works with Full Keyboard Access.

requirements.title: Liquid Glass and materials
requirements.criterion: Standard components supply Liquid Glass. It is not used in the content layer, custom glass is rare, the regular variant is the default, and custom backgrounds are not added to bars, popovers, or menu bar extra windows.

requirements.title: Semantic color
requirements.criterion: Colors use macOS dynamic system colors for their documented roles, are not hard-coded system values, mean one thing each, and respect the accent color people choose.

requirements.title: Light and dark appearance
requirements.criterion: Every view is legible in light and dark appearance, uses system label colors, and does not offer an app-specific appearance setting.

requirements.title: Typography
requirements.criterion: Text uses macOS text styles or system font variants, stays at or above the 10 pt minimum (13 pt default body), avoids light weights, and uses few typefaces.

requirements.title: SF Symbols
requirements.criterion: Symbols are familiar for their action, match adjacent text weight, use a rendering mode that works in every context, animate only with a clear purpose, and custom symbols have text labels.

requirements.title: Layout hierarchy
requirements.criterion: Content is ordered by importance, aligned for scanning, grouped by relation, controls are distinct from content, and spacing is consistent.

requirements.title: Purposeful motion
requirements.criterion: Motion is brief, purposeful, never the only carrier of information, and absent from interactions that happen often.

requirements.title: Text contrast
requirements.criterion: Text up to 17 pt that is not bold has at least 4.5:1 contrast against its rendered background, in each supported appearance.

requirements.title: Large or bold text contrast
requirements.criterion: Text of 18 pt or larger, or bold text, has at least 3:1 contrast against its rendered background.

requirements.title: Non-text contrast
requirements.criterion: Symbols, control boundaries, and state indicators that people need have at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors.

requirements.title: Increase Contrast
requirements.criterion: Custom colors provide a higher-contrast variant when Increase Contrast is on, in both appearances.

requirements.title: Not color alone
requirements.criterion: Status, severity, and state are shown with a shape, symbol, or text in addition to color.

requirements.title: macOS control size
requirements.criterion: Each pointer target has a hit region of at least 20 by 20 pt. Targets below the 28 by 28 pt default are reported as advice.

requirements.title: Space between targets
requirements.criterion: Adjacent controls are far enough apart that people do not hit the wrong one, even in a dense layout.

requirements.title: Name, role, value, and state
requirements.criterion: Every control and meaningful image exposes an accurate VoiceOver label, role, value, and state. Decorative images are hidden.

requirements.title: VoiceOver navigation
requirements.criterion: Headings, grouping, and reading order follow the visual hierarchy, and important content or layout changes are announced.

requirements.title: Text size
requirements.criterion: macOS has no Dynamic Type, so text uses text styles at or above 10 pt and layouts do not clip or overlap when content is long or localized.

requirements.title: Reduce Motion
requirements.criterion: With Reduce Motion on, automatic and repeating animations, zooms, and blurs are removed or replaced with fades, and no state is lost.

requirements.title: Reduce Transparency
requirements.criterion: Content and controls stay legible and distinct with Reduce Transparency on and over the least favorable content behind a material.

requirements.title: Time limits
requirements.criterion: Views do not dismiss on a timer. Any deliberate time limit, such as a safety expiry, is stated in plain words before it matters.

requirements.title: Writing
requirements.criterion: Labels and messages are concise, action oriented, and consistent. Errors say what happened and what to do next. Empty views give a next step.

requirements.title: Menu items
requirements.criterion: Menu items use title-style capitalization without articles, show an ellipsis when more input follows, appear dimmed when unavailable, and use icons for all items in a group or none.

requirements.title: Information density
requirements.criterion: Views are information dense, following Apple's compact menu bar extra pattern, and do not adopt roomier spacing for decoration.

requirements.title: No decorative card or pill chrome
requirements.criterion: Content is not wrapped in decorative cards, rounded boxes, or pill-shaped badges. Grouping uses alignment, spacing, separators, and system list or form styles.

requirements.title: No subtitle lines above sections
requirements.criterion: Sections do not have a light-gray subtitle or eyebrow line above their heading.

requirements.title: No em dashes in UI text
requirements.criterion: No user-visible string contains an em dash (U+2014).

requirements.title: No continuously repainting views
requirements.criterion: No view repaints on a timer while idle: no pulse, shimmer, blur, or spinner animation, no indefinite ProgressView, no repeating symbol effect, and no Text(date, style: .relative) or .timer text.

requirements.title: Menu bar glyph shows the worst finding
requirements.criterion: The menu bar glyph is a static symbol that encodes the worst current finding by shape, not by color or animation alone, and its accessibility label names that state.
